patents.source: USPTO Open Data Portal, granted patents since 2001, applicant phrase "xiaomi", 2026-10-06

reading.body:
Xiaomi is listed as a Chinese foundation model developer through MiMo, but the data records no compute, data center, or power footprint behind it.

The entry is a company record, not an infrastructure record. It establishes that a Beijing consumer hardware firm founded in 2010 and listed in Hong Kong has a foundation model product, and that cross-border data review is advised for it. Nothing here describes training clusters, accelerator counts, or electricity supply.

That gap is the point for AI scaling. A model can appear in a catalog of Chinese foundation models while the physical capacity that produced it stays invisible. If compute is the constraint, then a company page without compute figures cannot tell you whether MiMo is a serious training effort or a thin wrapper on someone else's capacity.

What the data does not cover: model size, training location, chip supply, or any partnership. It also does not say whether Xiaomi operates its own data centers. The verification date and the single product entry are the whole record, so treat this as a pointer to a company, not evidence about its scale.
